title: Cap. 7 Contra Sol. 2: God-side application; Scotus on joining the unjoined
pass_a_gloss: That this objection may be met, that saying of the Apostle is to be set as a foundation, Ephesians 1:3: God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ. That is, Whatever saving good descends to us from God is gifted to us through Christ and on account of Christ's merits. Since therefore saving faith itself, which is proper to the elect, is to be placed among the chief spiritual blessings, it is confessed that it is gifted on account of Christ's merits to all those to whom it is in fact gifted. What therefore the theologians commonly say, that faith is that instrument by means of which Christ's merits are applied to us, is to be understood of application considered from the side of human beings: For the elect themselves cannot apply Christ's merits to themselves for the perception of any spiritual benefits whatsoever, unless faith is presupposed in them. But if we consider application or imputation from the side of God alone, then it must be said that God both can and is accustomed to apply, that is, to impute and communicate, Christ's merits to human beings, so that with regard to these merits he gives them spiritual goods, even when they are counted as impious and unbelieving. For faith itself, when it is first given, is not given to a believer, but to an unbeliever: yet it is given to the elect on account of the Mediator's merits. It is necessary therefore that we confess that no one of the elect could by believing apply Christ's merits to himself for the fruit of eternal life, unless God from special mercy, on account of this merit of Christ, had first infused into them the faith by which they would believe. And this is that special application of Christ's merits which, from the special will of Christ offering himself, and of God the Father accepting this sacrifice, we affirm pertains to the elect by a certain peculiar privilege. Scotus looked to this in that saying most worthy of observation: This was chiefly in Christ's merit, that he merited that the unjoined be joined, book 3, distinction 19, unique question, page 75. Which is as if he had said that the chief efficacy of Christ's merits is situated in this, that he merited that certain ones from among unbelievers should in fact become faithful, and joined to Christ by faith should obtain eternal life. This is that special ordination of Christ's merits, and application, which wholly depends on God's good pleasure, not on human choice.
pass_b_english: To meet the objection, take Ephesians 1:3 as foundation: God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing in Christ — that is, every saving good that comes down from God is given through Christ and for his merits. Saving faith, proper to the elect, ranks among the chief spiritual blessings; so it is granted, for Christ's merits, to all who in fact receive it. When theologians say faith is the instrument by which Christ's merits are applied to us, they mean application on the human side: the elect cannot apply those merits to themselves for any spiritual benefit unless faith is already presupposed in them. But if we view application or imputation from God's side alone, God can and does apply — impute and communicate — Christ's merits to people so that, with regard to those merits, he gives spiritual goods even while they still count as ungodly and unbelieving. Faith, when first given, is not given to a believer but to an unbeliever; yet it is given to the elect for the Mediator's merits. So we must confess: no elect person could, by believing, apply Christ's merits to himself for eternal life's fruit unless God, from special mercy and for that merit of Christ, had first infused the faith by which they would believe. That is the special application of Christ's merits which, from Christ's special will in offering himself and the Father's in accepting the sacrifice, we say belongs to the elect by a peculiar privilege. Scotus saw this in a saying worth marking: the chief thing in Christ's merit was that he merited the joining of the unjoined (lib. 3, dist. 19, unique q., p. 75) — as if to say the main force of those merits is that some from among unbelievers should become believers and, joined to Christ by faith, obtain eternal life. That special ordination and application of Christ's merits hangs wholly on God's good pleasure, not on human choice.
source_text: Ut huic objectioni occurratur, fundamenti loco ponendum est illud Apostoli, Ephes. i. 3. Benedixit nobis Deus omni benedictione spirituali in Christo. Id est, Quicquid boni salutiferi ad nos a Deo descendit, id nobis per Christum & propter merita Christi donatur. Cum igitur ipsa fides salutifera, quae propria est electorum, sit inter praecipuas spirituales benedictiones reponenda, propter merita Christi illam donari iis omnibus, quibus de facto donatur, in confesso est. Quod igitur vulgo dicunt Theologi, fidem esse illud instrumentum, quo mediante merita Christi nobis applicantur, id intelligendum est de applicatione ex parte hominum considerata: Ipsi enim electi non possunt sibi applicare merita Christi ad perceptionem beneficiorum quorumcunque spiritualium, nisi fide in iis praesupposita. At si applicationem aut imputationem ex parte solius Dei consideremus, tum dicendum est, Deum & posse & solere applicare, id est, imputare & communicare, hominibus merita Christi, ita ut intuitu horum meritorum det illis bona spiritualia, etiam cum impii & infideles censeantur. Fides enim ipsa, cum primum datur, non fideli datur, sed infideli: datur autem electis propter merita Mediatoris. Necesse est ergo ut fateamur, neminem ex electis potuisse credendo sibi applicare merita Christi ad fructum vitae aeternae, nisi Deus ex speciali misericordia, propter hoc meritum Christi, fidem qua crederent illis prius infudisset. Atque haec est illa specialis applicatio meritorum Christi quam ex speciali voluntate Christi seipsum offerentis, Deique Patris hoc sacrificium acceptantis, ad electos peculiari quodam privilegio pertinere affirmamus. Scotus huc respexit, illo dicto observatione dignissimo, Haec fuit potissimum in merito Christi, quod meruit non-conjunctos conjungi, lib. 3. dist. 19. qu. unica, pag. 75. Quod perinde est ac si dixisset, praecipuam efficaciam meritorum Christi in eo sitam, quod meruit ut quidam ex infidelibus reapse fierent fideles, Christoque per fidem conjuncti vitam aeternam consequerentur. Haec est illa specialis ordinatio meritorum Christi, atque applicatio, quae tota pendet ex Dei beneplacito, non ex hominum arbitrio.
